deployment: theborg cicd namespace (concourse.home), configured by home-infra apps/concourse.yaml

web.tracing.uncovered: Spans go to the cluster's Tempo; the tier has no reader for them. testhelpers/otel asserts export end to end and is kept out of CI because it needs tempo.home and loki.home.

web.tls.note: TLS terminates at the Traefik ingress.

web.hangar.note: Strict Hangar inputs are off here. Turning them on is a deployment change, not a test one: artifactDaemon.hangar.enabled/webEnabled, a store (artifactDaemon.hangar.store gcs with artifactDaemon.hangar.bucket and endpoint pointed at the fake-gcs emulator, or disk via hangarStorage.disk), and a hangar.key in the pinned daemon TLS Secret. home-infra sets no artifactDaemon.hangar value since 5db877d. Hangar is covered by the hangar_live contracts in the k8s-e2e pipeline, on a throwaway K3s cluster, and the output plane's tier-2 conformance runs in unit-tests against the deployed fake-gcs.

web.hangarOutput.note: The Hangar output plane (the artifact daemon's publisher and execution control, and web's reclaim and orphan sweep) is not deployed here; see web.hangar.

web.hangarOutputCapture.note: Needs the output plane; see web.hangarOutput. hangarOutput.webEnabled is also what puts the plane in service (web writes its hangar_enabled row from it); there is no activation step. With it on, the named tests run a managed-input Run, a review Run and an implement Run on the disk store and download and verify each result against its binding (hangar_one_daemon A8); the workload tests also need CONCOURSE_LIVE_REVIEW_WORKER_IMAGE (the review worker with the fixture codex, pinned in web.runCredentialWorkerImages) and CONCOURSE_LIVE_VALIDATE_IMAGE.

daemon.hangarOutput.note: The output plane is mounted in the artifact daemon (its --control-key-file) from rollout step S6 of hangar_stores_enabled_in_cluster; see web.hangarOutput.

store.disk.note: The Hangar disk store (hangarStorage.disk) is initialized at rollout step S2 and runs from S3; see web.hangar.

daemon.hangar.note: See web.hangar. The persistent-disk Hangar store (hangarStorage.disk, cmd/hangar-store) is off here too, by decision: its live coverage is the hangar_live contract TestLiveHangarDiskStoreRoundTripSurvivesRestart (live_hangar_disk_test.go), run by the hangar-disk-store-contract job in deploy/k8s-e2e-pipeline.yml on a throwaway K3s cluster, not a flag flipped on this cluster. It deploys the chart-rendered hangar-store on a PVC and the artifact daemon with strict inputs on disk, and proves publish, materialization by a generated step pod, and a hangar-store pod restart that keeps the tree ref and never reissues a generation.

daemon.durableStore.note: No durable resource-cache store is configured here; cmd/artifact-daemon/durable covers the cache wrapper against fake-gcs-server and a real disk store, and brine's daemon-durable feature drives the real daemon against a GCS emulator.

daemon.mirrorReplicas.uncovered: Mirroring copies each output to a peer daemon. This cluster has two daemon nodes (daemon.nodes), but k3s-agent-y is a desktop VM that sleeps, so mirroring is live only while it is up and no live test can count on a peer. Cross-node mirroring is covered by cmd/artifact-daemon's behavioral_cross_node_test.go with two daemons on one host; cross-node artifact handoff on this cluster by brine's live-multinode tier, which runs only when both nodes are up.

daemon.nodes.uncovered: Not a feature: asserted so a change in how many nodes run a daemon -- which decides whether mirroring has a peer -- fails this test until daemon.mirrorReplicas says what covers it. Counted from the registered nodes the DaemonSet can place on, so a node that is asleep (NotReady) still counts.
